outcomes.text: Understand brief recordings about routine needs, such as shopping, directions and simple instructions.
Work out the meaning of occasional unfamiliar words and phrases from context.
Understand short, straightforward texts such as public signs, notices and travel information.
Locate main points, particular information and details in predictable practical texts.
Infer the meaning of occasional unfamiliar words and expressions from context.
Communicate reasonably accurately using varied relevant grammar, tenses and vocabulary.
Write with reasonable accuracy using varied relevant structures, time frames and vocabulary.
Use -mente adverbs, common adverbs, and adverbial expressions for manner, time, place and degree.
Form comparisons and superlatives with adjectives and adverbs, including irregular and -ísimo forms.
Form questions using Spanish interrogatives for what, how much, which, who, when, where, how, why and purpose.
Use regular, irregular, reflexive and stem-changing verbs in all persons and numbers.
Form negative statements with common negative words and expressions.
Use se in impersonal expressions such as se puede, se necesita and se habla.
Distinguish common uses of ser and estar.
Use common expressions with tener, impersonal verbs and weather verbs.
Use the present indicative, present continuous, preterite, imperfect and imperfect continuous.
Use the immediate future, future, perfect, pluperfect and conditional.
Use the gerund, passive voice and common imperative forms.
Recognise present-subjunctive forms in exclamations and formal positive or negative commands.
Use the present subjunctive after expressions of wishing, commands, requests, emotion, purpose and future time.
Use the imperfect subjunctive in forms such as quisiera and si fuera.
Use common Spanish prepositions, including the personal a.
Join ideas with coordinating and subordinating conjunctions, including y, o, pero, sino, porque, cuando, mientras and si.
Use cardinal and ordinal numbers, quantities, dates, days, months, years and times, including the 24-hour clock.
Use desde hace with present and imperfect tenses.
Understand and use common Spanish adjectives, including their feminine and plural forms where applicable.
Understand and use common adverbs and prepositions for place, possibility, frequency, manner, emphasis and qualification.
Understand and use cardinal, ordinal and fractional numbers and other expressions of quantity.
Understand and use expressions for sequence, frequency, duration, relative time, days, parts of the day and clock time.
Understand and use common verbs covering communication, movement, activities, feelings, opinions, relationships and everyday actions.
Deduce the meanings of unfamiliar Spanish words from context on familiar topics.
Recognise both old and revised spellings accepted under Spanish spelling reforms.
Understand factual information and ideas in announcements, messages, news, interviews and dialogues about familiar subjects.
Find main points, specific facts and details in recordings about personal life, shopping, school, work and leisure.
Understand simple accounts of events, opinions, feelings, hopes and ambitions.
Understand simple written accounts of events, views, emotions, hopes and ambitions.
Hold spontaneous conversations about familiar personal interests and everyday subjects.
Use pronunciation and intonation features to express meaning and attitude.
Know Spanish noun gender and singular and plural forms.
Use definite and indefinite articles, including al, del and lo with adjectives.
Use adjective agreement, position, demonstrative adjectives and possessive adjectives.
Use subject, direct-object, indirect-object, prepositional, reflexive, possessive, relative and demonstrative pronouns.
Use indefinite forms such as algo, alguien, alguno, mucho, poco, tanto, todo, cualquiera and otro.
Take part in brief social exchanges and communicate about familiar needs, including shopping, food, transport and directions.
Connect short points into a sequence using simple linking words.
Use suitable conversational strategies to keep an interaction going.
Complete forms with simple personal details.
Write simple factual information using everyday vocabulary and expressions.
Link simple phrases and sentences about personal life, surroundings and everyday matters.
Produce connected texts about familiar topics such as arrangements, preferences, family, education, work and travel.
Use simple connectors to join shorter points into a coherent sequence.
Talk about past events, experiences, hopes and ambitions, giving short reasons for opinions and plans.
Describe past experiences, opinions, hopes and ambitions, with brief reasons for views and plans.
Recognise main points, themes, opinions, ideas, feelings and attitudes in predictable spoken texts.
Understand authentic articles, emails, blogs and letters about familiar subjects and situations.
Identify themes, opinions, ideas, feelings and attitudes in predictable written texts.
Know vocabulary for digital devices, online communication, files, websites, social media and online safety.
Know verbs and expressions for using the internet, handling digital content and publishing online.
Know vocabulary for documents, written texts, printed materials, correspondence and qualifications.
Know vocabulary for natural features, environmental issues, landscapes, resources and weather-related surroundings.
Know verbs and expressions for helping, conserving, reducing, reusing and protecting the environment.
Know vocabulary for temperatures, weather conditions, seasons and weather forecasts.
Know Spanish names for common animals.
Know vocabulary for public buildings, services, educational establishments, leisure facilities and transport buildings.
Know vocabulary for urban areas, roads, traffic, public transport and street features.
Know vocabulary for shops, shopping places, customers, prices, payment and purchasing goods.
Know verbs and expressions for shopping, paying, returning goods, complaining and obtaining refunds.
Know Spanish units for measuring temperature, weight, distance, volume and length.
Know adjectives describing size, height and length.
Know vocabulary for common shapes and related shape adjectives.
Know vocabulary for common materials, including metals, fabrics, wood, plastic, glass and paper.

subtopics.title: Las personas y los lugares – Los puntos cardinales

outcomes.text: Know Spanish vocabulary for the four cardinal directions.

subtopics.title: Los países, las nacionalidades y los idiomas

outcomes.text: Know how to discuss one’s first language, other studied languages, nationality, residence and Spanish-speaking countries.
Know vocabulary for schools, nurseries, secondary institutions and universities.
Know vocabulary for learners, courses, school years, departments, staff, education and school facilities.
Know vocabulary for classroom equipment and learning tools.
Know Spanish names for school subjects.
Know vocabulary for studying, lessons, classmates, homework, examinations, tasks, results and grades.
Know verbs and expressions for studying, understanding, answering, revising, taking notes and achieving results.
Know vocabulary for a wide range of occupations and professions.
Know vocabulary for workplaces, employers, employees, jobs, pay, organisations, businesses and strikes.
Know verbs and expressions for finding, obtaining, applying for, starting, leaving and losing employment.

subtopics.title: La cultura – las costumbres, las creencias y las celebraciones

outcomes.text: Know vocabulary for religious beliefs, customs, festivals, national celebrations, birthdays and major holidays.
Know expressions for celebrating, believing, having faith and describing religious identity.
Learn vocabulary for meals, snacks and different types of food, including vegetarian and vegan meals.
Learn names for common fruits and vegetables.
Learn vocabulary for meat, fish and seafood.
Learn vocabulary for staple foods, ingredients, seasonings and other foods.
Learn vocabulary for snacks, cakes, sweets, toast, yoghurt and related foods.
Learn vocabulary for drinks, including water, coffee, tea, juice and soft drinks.
Use verbs and expressions for eating, drinking, preparing and cutting food, and expressing hunger or thirst.
Use adjectives to describe food as bitter, cooked, raw, sweet, fresh, spicy, tasty or salty.
Learn vocabulary for cutlery, crockery and kitchen utensils.
Learn vocabulary for major body parts.
Use verbs and expressions for hearing, smelling, tasting, touching, breathing, feeling and taking a break.
Learn vocabulary for medical appointments, healthcare workers, medicines and basic medical supplies.
Use expressions for illness, injuries, symptoms, exercise, treatment and general wellbeing.
Learn vocabulary for vehicles, travel documents, luggage, journeys, stations, tickets, directions and travellers.

subtopics.title: Los viajes y los transportes – Verbos y expresiones

outcomes.text: Use verbs and expressions for travelling, driving, walking, boarding, arriving, turning, following directions and flying.
Use greetings, farewells, apologies, thanks, questions and common conversational phrases.
Use exclamations to express welcome, admiration, interest, annoyance, regret or sympathy.
Invite someone, suggest activities, express willingness and accept or refuse an invitation.
Learn vocabulary for family members, ages, relationships, marital status, childhood and personal identity.
Use verbs for adoption, growing up, raising children, spelling names, pregnancy, birth, death and residence.
Use vocabulary to describe height, build, age, hair, eyes, facial hair, clothing accessories and physical appearance.
Use adjectives and nouns to describe personality, emotions, mood, behaviour and personal qualities.
Use verbs for showing affection, causing emotions, liking, becoming angry, laughing, smiling, worrying and reacting.
Learn vocabulary for rooms, household structures, entrances, stairs, walls, floors, ceilings and windows.
Learn vocabulary for living-room furniture and objects.
Learn vocabulary for bathroom fixtures, toiletries, towels, mirrors and personal-care items.
Use verbs for bathing, showering, washing, brushing teeth, applying makeup and combing hair.
Learn vocabulary for kitchen containers, furniture and appliances.
Use verbs for cooking, heating, freezing, washing, cleaning, cutting, frying, boiling and preparing meals.
Learn vocabulary for bedroom furniture and items, including beds, pillows, blankets, wardrobes and lamps.
Use verbs and expressions for going to bed, waking up, sleeping, resting, getting up and feeling tired.
Use expressions for washing clothes, cleaning, vacuuming, ironing, setting or clearing the table and taking out rubbish.
Learn vocabulary for gardens, plants, trees, grass, flowers and garden walls.
Use expressions for maintaining a garden, growing plants and planting flowers or vegetables.
Learn vocabulary for household appliances, heating, electricity, gas, telephones, radios and televisions.
Use verbs for opening, closing, switching appliances on or off, pushing, calling, repairing, breaking and throwing.
Learn names and descriptive terms for common colours and shades.
Learn vocabulary for clothing, footwear, accessories, sizes, styles, materials and garments for different occasions.
Use expressions for wearing, putting on, taking off, trying on and describing how clothes fit or look.
Talk about leisure activities such as listening to music, concerts, festivals, reading and watching television or films.
Learn vocabulary and expressions for hobbies including music, drawing, photography, gardening, fishing, painting, games and instruments.
Learn vocabulary for sports, athletes, equipment, teams, competitions, venues, results and sporting activities.
